collection.description: A child asks where the tribe came from: hear another version, search for evidence, or accept the unknown.

q1.name: Where did we come from?
q1.text:
A child asks an elder, "Where did our people come from?" Several adults give different accounts.
Some say a volcanic explosion forced our ancestors to flee their old home. Their vessels were swept away, and the survivors washed ashore here.
Another elder says the sea itself guided the boats toward safety.
A skeptical historian says the story may combine several migrations.

choices.label: Ask an elder to tell another version.
Search for records or physical evidence.
Accept that some questions may remain unanswered.

q2.name: Where did we come from?
q2.text:
A child asks an elder, "Where did our people come from?" Several adults give different accounts.
The story says two villagers fell down a waterfall and met the other founders, who may or may not have been children.
Some insist the founders were already living here before the fall.
Another version says the waterfall was remembered as an entrance, not the whole story of how the settlement began.

choices.label: Ask an elder to tell another version.
Search for records or physical evidence.
Accept that some questions may remain unanswered.

q3.name: Where did we come from?
q3.text:
A child asks an elder, "Where did our people come from?" Several adults give different accounts.
Our ancestors may have become lost while seeking the Southern Shore.
Others say they deliberately came north to expand the population.
A third tradition claims they followed signs left by earlier inhabitants.

choices.label: Ask an elder to tell another version.
Search for records or physical evidence.
Accept that some questions may remain unanswered.

q4.name: Where did we come from?
q4.text:
A child asks an elder, "Where did our people come from?" Several adults give different accounts.
Supposedly {@chief} noticed troubling ecological, magical or spiritual signs of collapse and instructed our ancestors to travel here.
Another version says they became lost and found this place by chance.
Some say a mysterious force guided them to the Tree.

choices.label: Ask an elder to tell another version.
Search for records or physical evidence.
Accept that some questions may remain unanswered.

text_only.reason: a legend of the ancestors' old home; no building collapses

q5.name: Where did we come from?
q5.text:
A child asks an elder, "Where did our people come from?" Several adults give different accounts.
Perhaps our ancestors were captured and brought here.
Perhaps they discovered the place by accident.
Perhaps someone among the Heathens invited or warned them to come.
Some say the settlement was already divided before anyone arrived.

choices.label: Ask an elder to tell another version.
Search for records or physical evidence.
Accept that some questions may remain unanswered.

o1.name: Outcome 1
o1.text: The child learns that history can contain uncertainty and disagreement.

o2.name: Outcome 2
o2.text: A researcher gains a modest History/Research experience increment.

o3.name: Outcome 3
o3.text: A storyteller records a new variant for later retelling.

o4.name: Outcome 4
